results.notes: Source: Ju and Aral, Collaborating with AI Agents, arXiv 2503.18238v3, February 2026; complete paper and Appendices A-L read. Printed benchmarks were checked directly in PDF p. 16 (Table 1 and 11,024 ads), p. 22 (50% increase), and p. 47 (Table B, Individual, Demographics No). The control level printed as Intercept is compared as an intercept, not relabeled as a printed descriptive mean. The supplied OSF deposit is titled Personality Pairing Improves Human-AI Collaboration; its hh_benchmark.csv covers both arms of this experiment, whereas most other files cover Human-AI only. Outcome: hh_benchmark.csv submission_count, one row per unique participant_id; treatment is human-ai and control is human-human. Retain the complete analyzed cohort, with the paper's exclusions already reflected in these rows; introduce no additional exclusions. Missing submission counts (36 Human-AI, 153 Human-Human) are zero counts for people absent from the submission aggregation, not grounds to remove them. Every such row also lacks ad_quality_index. This zero interpretation is supported by exact equality between all Human-AI benchmark counts and distinct rated ads per creator, including zeros, and reproduces the full-sample intercept, coefficient, standard errors, total ads, and percentage. Dropping missing counts instead would leave only 2,045 people. The broader submissions.csv has 7,537 Human-AI ad records, including 271 absent from the 7,266 distinct ads in ad_ratings.csv; use the benchmark's analysis counts, not that broader creator-map count. The original filter explaining these 271 records is not included in the deposit. Preserve the posted attribution of submissions to each person; do not assign each jointly made ad to both human partners. Productivity is already a participant total, so no output/rater averaging is appropriate. Sample SDs use denominator n-1. Reproduction uses OLS with intercept and arm indicator; HC1 matches the paper's robust SE at three decimals, although the paper does not identify a specific HC variant. The requested difference is the unadjusted Human-AI minus Human-Human mean, with HC2 OLS SE. HC2 was independently checked against sqrt(s1^2/n1 + s0^2/n0). Assignment was individual before partner matching (PDF p. 14), so n_clusters is null. HC2 does not additionally model dependence between Human-Human partners; their membership identifiers are unavailable. This is a between-person experiment, so there is no paired or first_round result.

skipped.reason: The deposit omits ad copy and embeddings. PDF p. 21 requires the original headline, primary text, and description embedded with text-embedding-3-small, distances to each arm's centroid, and a text-submitting sample of 2,034 people. Neither those texts nor the vectors nor the published diversity scores are available. The exact set-based procedure cannot be reproduced; no substitute embedding model, participant SD, or diversity effect is computed.

Table 2 (PDF p. 22) reports 45,803 human-rating observations and an adjusted text coefficient of 0.327. ad_ratings.csv contains only 30,126 ratings on 7,266 ads from 1,222 Human-AI creators; there are no Human-Human ratings. hh_benchmark.csv contains only a combined ad_quality_index, not the separate text/image/click outcomes. Full-sample linked age and sex covariates are also unavailable. The published contrast cannot be reproduced, and the composite is not substituted for this outcome.

The complete participant counts and submission outcome are available, but the Table 2/Table B model requires linked age, gender, and Big Five covariates. hh_benchmark.csv lacks age and sex. participants.csv has sex and coarsened age_band for Human-AI only. randomization_balance.csv has age and sex_male but no participant key; the deposit README explicitly states these covariates cannot be re-linked. Row order is not a valid linkage. Consequently the printed adjusted coefficient 1.954 cannot be reproduced. The separately reproduced unadjusted coefficient 1.925 is not used to claim reproduction of this model.

Table B (PDF p. 47) analyzes 1,751 teams (Table 1: 1,258 Human-AI and 493 Human-Human). The deposit has no Human-Human team/session membership or Human-Human submission-to-team mapping; the session identifiers in other files cover Human-AI only. Participant submission totals alone cannot recover team outcomes or the allocation of joint team outcomes to participants. The paper's 976 Human-Human people also do not equal twice its 493 teams. Thus team counts, the team regression, and participant-level dispersion cannot be independently reproduced from this deposit. No synthetic pairing or doubling of individual counts is used.

Table H (PDF p. 52) uses 11,024 evaluations by gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18. The deposit supplies human rater IDs and repeated human ratings, but no AI-rating dataset for either arm, and omits the ad copy and images needed to evaluate the original mockups. The available human ratings/composite cannot reproduce the printed AI-rating coefficient 0.128; no replacement model evaluations are generated.

The deposit omits headline content and completion indicators/rates. submissions.csv contains only creator and ad identifiers. The paper's Table E (PDF p. 49) does not specify the rate denominator or coding procedure, and full-sample demographic covariates cannot be linked. The completion variable in field_docsend.csv measures subsequent report viewing, not completion of ad copy. This estimate cannot be reproduced.
